title: Ada and the Blue Hour
premise: Ada Pemberton has spent three years in a marriage measured in millimeters, her husband Edmund inspecting bridges while she practices the art of almost leaving. When a late-night radio program broadcasts a song her late mother wrote and never recorded — a song that exists only in the family's burned notebooks — Ada realizes someone kept copies, and that person knows why her mother's estate was settled so unjustly decades ago. She returns to Harrow Bend before the sale of her childhood house closes, confronting the uncle who took everything and discovering the song was recorded once, secretly, by the man her mother loved. In the blue hour of the last morning, Ada chooses testimony over inheritance: she gives the recording to the radio station and the house to the town, walking out with something no deed can hold.
about_author: Coral Ashgrove is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent fifteen years mapping property lines across the American South before turning to fiction. Her work examines what documents can and cannot settle, and she writes each novel longhand in the hour before dawn.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A bridge inspection in the rain becomes an accidental audit of his marriage: every gap he measures reminds him of what he almost said on their wedding day. That night, half-asleep beside Ada, he hears a radio song he doesn't recognize — and watches his wife sit bolt upright, white-faced, whispering that it's her mother's handwriting made audible. The beat: dread disguised as domestic routine.

chapters.title: The Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She traces the broadcast to a small AM station in Harrow Bend and learns the DJ received a cassette from an anonymous donor — one of three, mailed from inside the family. Flashbacks reveal how Uncle Raymond had the notebooks burned after her mother's death and settled the estate against her father. Edmund offers to come; she refuses, and the refusal lands like a door. The beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Harrow Bend, Closing Time
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ada arrives as the house sale enters its final week; Raymond, charming and failing, controls both the deed and the story everyone tells about her mother. She finds the second cassette hidden in the piano bench with a letter naming the man who recorded it — and evidence Raymond forged her mother's signature. When he discovers her searching, the confrontation turns physical, then legal: he threatens to contest everything she'd inherit. The beat: rising danger, justice slipping out of lawful reach.

chapters.title: Blue Hour
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, closing with Edmund's letter read aloud. Rather than fight for the house or expose Raymond through courts that failed her mother, Ada plays the third cassette on the morning radio show — her mother's voice, finally public — and signs the deed over to the town as a music room. Raymond is left holding paper worth nothing but its shame. Driving home at dawn, she calls Edmund and finishes the sentence from their wedding day. The beat: release, belonging chosen rather than inherited.
